signals.label: HHS — Medicaid Grants to States
signals.description: Federal Medicaid grants to states. Direct funding for cancer patients on Medicaid.
signals.advocacy_note: Medicaid is the primary payer for cancer care in low-income populations. YoY declines signal direct reductions in cancer care access funding.
signals.explanation: MTD spending is +32.5% vs same period last year ($47,416M vs $35,774M). Expansion exceeds +5% threshold.
signals.category_match: HHS - Grants to States for Medicaid

signals.label: Medicare Part A — Hospital Insurance Trust Fund
signals.description: Federal Hospital Insurance Trust Fund payments. Covers inpatient cancer treatment.
signals.advocacy_note: Medicare Part A covers inpatient hospital stays for cancer treatment. YoY changes reflect shifts in hospital utilization and reimbursement.
signals.explanation: MTD spending is +294.9% vs same period last year ($35,158M vs $8,902M). Expansion exceeds +5% threshold.
signals.category_match: HHS - Federal Hospital Insr Trust Fund

signals.label: Medicare Part B — Supplemental Medical Insurance
signals.description: Federal Supplemental Medical Insurance Trust Fund. Covers outpatient chemo and physician services.
signals.advocacy_note: Medicare Part B covers outpatient chemotherapy, physician visits, and diagnostic imaging. This is the primary federal payment channel for oncology drug administration.
signals.explanation: MTD spending is +375.7% vs same period last year ($50,332M vs $10,581M). Expansion exceeds +5% threshold.
signals.category_match: HHS - Federal Supple Med Insr Trust Fund

signals.label: Medicare Prescription Drugs (Part D)
signals.description: Medicare prescription drug program payments. Covers oral cancer drugs.
signals.advocacy_note: Medicare Part D covers oral cancer medications. YoY changes reflect drug cost trends and utilization shifts.
signals.explanation: MTD spending is +109542.9% vs same period last year ($15,350M vs $14M). Expansion exceeds +5% threshold.

signals.label: NIH — National Institutes of Health
signals.description: NIH funding disbursements. Includes NCI cancer research grants.
signals.advocacy_note: NIH funds the National Cancer Institute and cancer research grants. YoY declines signal reduced cancer research investment. Note: NIH disbursements are grant-cycle driven and back-loaded — mid-month MTD comparisons (before day 22) are unreliable.

signals.label: ACA Marketplace Payments
signals.description: ACA health insurance marketplace payments. Covers subsidized coverage for cancer patients.
signals.advocacy_note: ACA marketplace payments fund subsidized health insurance. Payments are monthly lump-sum settlements. A ±3 day window is used for prior year comparison to account for business day variation.

thresholds.rationale: 5% YoY decline is operationally significant for federal health programs

limitations: DTS data reflects cash flows, not accruals. Payment timing can shift MTD values.
Large single-day payments (e.g., ACA Marketplace monthly settlements) can distort MTD.
YoY comparison assumes consistent payment timing between years — not always true.
